Temperature (°C = (°F - 32) / 1.8): -40°F = -40°C; -32°F = -36°C; -25°F = -32°C; -10°F = -23°C; -4°F = -20°C; 0°F = -18°C; 15°F = -9°C; 23°F = -5°C; 32°F = 0°C; 122°F = 50°C; 140°F = 60°C; 150°F = 66°C; 158°F = 70°C; 160°F = 71°C; 176°F = 80°C; 200°F = 93°C; 350°F = 177°C; 400°F = 204°C; 450°F = 232°C.
extraFacts.source: NIST SP 811 unit conversion; 1 bar = 14.5038 psi

extraFacts.fact: NPT is the American taper pipe thread to ASME B1.20.1 and NPTF is the dryseal version to ASME B1.20.3; BSPP (G) is parallel pipe thread to ISO 228-1 and BSPT (R) is taper pipe thread to ISO 7-1. NPT and BSP threads do not mate. FNPT is female NPT and MNPT is male NPT.
extraFacts.source: ASME B1.20.1; ASME B1.20.3; ISO 228-1; ISO 7-1

extraFacts.fact: HS 2022 heading 84.81 covers taps, cocks and valves: subheading 8481.20 valves for oleohydraulic or pneumatic transmissions, 8481.30 check (non-return) valves, 8481.40 safety or relief valves, 8481.80 other appliances. The importing country's tariff fixes the final national digits.
ISO 4414 sets the general rules and safety requirements for pneumatic fluid power systems, including that stored pressure be able to be isolated and exhausted before work on the machine.
extraFacts.source: ISO 4414:2010 Pneumatic fluid power - General rules and safety requirements for systems and their components

extraFacts.fact: Meter-out speed control throttles the air leaving the cylinder and gives steady speed under varying load, the normal choice for double-acting cylinders; meter-in throttles the supply air. A quick exhaust valve dumps cylinder exhaust air at the valve instead of through the long return line, so the piston moves faster. A check (non-return) valve passes air in one direction only; a piloted non-return valve opens in the blocked direction when a pilot signal is applied. A needle valve gives fine adjustment of flow with a tapered needle.
extraFacts.source: SMC Best Pneumatics catalogue, Flow Control Equipment technical data; Legris pneumatic catalogue

extraFacts.fact: In Legris flow-control part numbers the last two digits give the thread: 10 = 1/8, 13 = 1/4, 17 = 3/8, 21 = 1/2 (BSPT on speed controls, BSPP on piloted non-return valves), and the middle two digits give the tube OD in mm (04, 06, 08, 10, 12).
extraFacts.source: Legris pneumatic flow control catalogue, part numbers 7665 06 13, 7065 10 21, 7892 10 21 (rows in Indus size tables)

extraFacts.fact: In Numatics flow control swivel part numbers the first digit gives the male thread (0 = 10-32 UNF, 1 = 1/8 NPT, 2 = 1/4 NPT) and a trailing number gives the push-in tube size (4 = 1/8 inch, 5 = 5/32 inch, 8 = 1/4 inch, 12 = 3/8 inch).
